statement: After a Debug pass, the next iteration's Exercise pass is dispatched only for the representative criterion of each cause that Debug pass addressed; no other open build-defect criterion appears in that iteration's Exercise dispatch
evidence: jest run transcript of the workflow test that drives the script with stubbed agents through a Debug pass addressing one of several causes, showing a passing assertion that the next iteration's Exercise slices hold exactly the addressed causes' representative ids

statement: In an iteration after a Debug pass, an open criterion that was not dispatched to Exercise is not re-judged: it reaches the Judge as "open, not re-checked this iteration" and its status and cause in verification-state.json are unchanged from the previous iteration
cites: §Objectives line 24 ("No other open criterion is exercised or re-judged"); §Intended Change lines 69-70
evidence: jest run transcript showing a passing assertion that an un-dispatched open criterion keeps its prior status and cause after the targeted iteration, and that the Judge input labels it open and not re-checked

statement: An evidence-gap re-capture that F-1 already schedules is still dispatched in an iteration after a Debug pass, alongside the addressed causes' representatives
cites: §Objectives line 24 ("plus any evidence-gap re-capture F-1 already schedules"); §Intended Change lines 68-69
evidence: jest run transcript showing a passing assertion that a targeted iteration's Exercise dispatch contains both the representative ids and the id of a criterion pending its one evidence-gap re-capture

statement: The first iteration of every invocation (a fresh run, a resume, a /verify-build fix round) exercises the whole open set; targeting applies only after a Debug pass within the same invocation
evidence: jest run transcript showing passing assertions that iteration 1 of a fresh run and of a resumed run (resume snapshot supplied) dispatches every open criterion to Exercise

statement: The Judge returns a cause key on every build-defect criterion it rules, and criteria the Judge rules to share a root cause carry the same key and are grouped by the workflow into one cause
evidence: jest run transcript showing passing assertions that the Judge schema requires a cause key on build-defect criteria, and that criteria returned with one shared key form a single cause in the workflow's cause map

statement: A build-defect criterion returned by the Judge with a missing or malformed cause key becomes its own cause, keyed `criterion:<id>`, and the substitution is logged
evidence: jest run transcript showing a passing assertion that a build-defect criterion with no cause key (and one with a malformed key) is recorded under key `criterion:<id>`, with the log line naming it

statement: verification-state.json records every cause with its key, its members and its representative (a top-level `causes` key), and each build-defect criterion's entry carries its `causeKey`
evidence: jest run transcript showing a passing assertion on the state file written after a judged iteration: a `causes` entry with key, members and representative, and `causeKey` on each member's criterion entry

statement: verification-report.md shows a Causes section listing each cause's key, members and representative
evidence: jest run transcript of the report renderer given a state with at least two causes, showing a passing assertion that the rendered report contains a Causes section naming each key, its members and its representative

statement: Each cause's representative is chosen deterministically: the first member in success-definition order that is not check-derived, or, if every member is check-derived, the first member; the choice is the same on every iteration for the same membership, and the workflow and the library choose the same representative for the same input
evidence: jest run transcript showing passing assertions on representative selection for (a) a cause with a check-derived first member and a non-check later member, (b) an all-check-derived cause, and a passing parity assertion between the workflow's rule and the library's

statement: A check-derived criterion (`derivation: check:<skill>`) is exercised in an iteration after a Debug pass only when it is its cause's representative, which happens only when every member of its cause is check-derived
evidence: jest run transcript showing a passing assertion that a targeted iteration does not dispatch a check-derived member of a mixed cause, and does dispatch the check-derived representative of an all-check cause

statement: Debug receives one gap per open cause, carrying the representative's evidence plus the members' functional statements, rather than one gap per criterion
evidence: jest run transcript showing a passing assertion that, for a cause of several members, the Debug prompt carries one gap for that cause holding the representative's evidence path and every member's statement

statement: A cause with many members (for example 20 criteria) is re-checked in the inner loop through exactly one representative: in an iteration after Debug addressed it, exactly one of its members is dispatched to Exercise
evidence: jest run transcript with a stubbed 20-member cause showing a passing assertion that the targeted iteration's Exercise dispatch holds exactly one id from that cause, the representative

statement: When a cause's representative is judged met, the cause closes and its other members are marked `awaiting: "regression"`; they are not dispatched to Exercise or re-judged in any later inner-loop iteration
evidence: jest run transcript showing passing assertions that after the representative is judged met, the cause is recorded closed, each other member carries `awaiting: "regression"` in the state, and none appears in a later inner-loop Exercise dispatch

statement: Members awaiting the regression pass are excluded from the gaps the next-step decision counts, so a closed cause's other members do not hold the loop open to the iteration cap
cites: §Intended Change lines 72-73; §Decision line 122 ("absorbed: decideNext excluding awaiting members from gaps")
evidence: jest run transcript of the next-step decision (library and `decide-next` CLI) showing a passing assertion that awaiting members are removed from both current and previous gaps, and that a run whose only remaining non-met criteria are awaiting does not return `remediate`

statement: When a representative is judged failing under a different cause key, its old cause closes, that cause's other members are marked awaiting the regression pass, and the representative becomes a member of the new cause
cites: §Decision lines 97-98 (Decision 3: "met, or now failing under a different key"); §Open Questions line 168 (OQ-4)
evidence: jest run transcript showing a passing assertion that, after the representative's key changes, the old cause is closed with its other members awaiting and the representative is listed under the new key

statement: When the loop reaches an exit other than `exit-unbuilt` or `exit-setup-failure` and members are awaiting the regression pass, the workflow runs exactly one Exercise and Judge pass over only those members, outside the iteration cap, with no Debug after it; criteria already met are not re-checked in it
cites: §Intended Change lines 76-78; §Decision lines 99-106 (Decision 4); §Decision line 121 (absorbed confirmation pass)
evidence: jest run transcript showing passing assertions that the exit pass dispatches Exercise for exactly the awaiting member ids (no met criterion), runs once, dispatches no Debug, and does not run at `exit-unbuilt` or `exit-setup-failure`

statement: An awaiting member judged still failing in the exit confirmation pass keeps the run from ending `satisfied`, and that pass's next-step decision is made with the cap set to the current iteration so it can never return `remediate`
evidence: jest run transcript showing a passing assertion that a member judged not met in the confirmation pass yields an outcome other than `satisfied`, and that the `decide-next` payload of that pass carries `cap` equal to the current iteration

statement: Members of a cause the last Debug pass did not address stay open and untouched: neither the representative nor any other member is dispatched to Exercise or re-judged in the next iteration, and each keeps its last verdict
evidence: jest run transcript with two causes, Debug addressing only one, showing passing assertions that no member of the unaddressed cause is in the next Exercise dispatch and each member's status and cause are unchanged in the state file

statement: Debug may return a pre-check (`command`, `exitCode`) per cause; a failing pre-check (non-zero exit code) marks the cause not addressed, so its representative is not re-captured that iteration
evidence: jest run transcript showing a passing assertion that a cause whose Debug return carries a pre-check with a non-zero exit code is absent from the next iteration's Exercise dispatch

statement: A passing pre-check never settles a criterion met: the representative is still re-captured and judged, the pre-check reaches Exercise only as a hint, and the Judge's prompt never contains it
cites: §Objectives line 30 ("only the criterion's own evidence, judged, does"); §Decision lines 107-109 (Decision 5)
evidence: jest run transcript showing passing assertions that a cause with a zero-exit pre-check still has its representative dispatched to Exercise, the Judge prompt does not contain the pre-check command, and the representative's status comes only from the Judge's ruling

statement: The next-step decision counts closed causes as well as closed criteria: given current and previous causes it reports the causes closed since the previous iteration, and it returns stalled only when neither a criterion nor a cause closed, so an iteration that closes a cause with no criterion status change is not stalled
evidence: jest run transcript of the library and the `decide-next` CLI showing passing assertions that a payload with unchanged gaps but one fewer cause returns the closed cause and not `exit-stalled`, and that one with neither closed returns `exit-stalled`

statement: When the Judge returns `exit-stalled` but the script's own cause map shows a cause closed that iteration, the script overrides the stall and the loop continues
evidence: jest run transcript showing a passing assertion that a stubbed Judge `exit-stalled` is overridden when the script's cause map records a closed cause

statement: The inner loop stays bounded by the existing iteration cap: no targeted iteration runs beyond it, and the exit confirmation pass adds no inner-loop round
cites: §Objectives line 31; §Decision lines 101-106 (Decision 4: "outside the iteration cap", "adds no extra inner-loop round")
evidence: jest run transcript showing a passing assertion that a run whose causes never close stops at the cap with the existing cap outcome, and that the count of inner-loop Exercise dispatches never exceeds the cap

statement: A headless run in the fixtures environment, seeded with two causes spread over at least six criteria with one cause fixed and one not, produces a verification-state.json whose second iteration's `exercised` entry lists only the fixed cause's representative; the state file also carries the `exercised` history (one entry per iteration) and the `causes` record, and a resume built from that state file still reads only `iteration`, `criteria` and `gapsClosed`
evidence: the fixture run's verification-state.json, whose `exercised` array's second entry holds exactly one id, the fixed cause's representative; plus a jest run transcript showing a passing assertion that a resume snapshot built from a state file carrying `exercised` and `causes` matches one built without them
